headline: Fixable before launch. As-is the model estimates 24%, but the actions below can reach ~66% — above the 33% bar. Do them before you go live.
focus_first: Shorten your campaign from 29 to 15 days
Lower your funding goal from $30,516 to $5,000

action_plan.action: Shorten your campaign from 29 to 15 days
action_plan.why: Campaign length materially shifts funding odds; a tighter window concentrates backer momentum.
action_plan.evidence: Games campaigns with a <=15d campaign funded at 66% vs a 40% baseline (lift 1.62, n=1,331).

action_plan.action: Lower your funding goal from $30,516 to $5,000
action_plan.why: The funding goal is the single strongest lever on fundability — right-sizing it to a category-proven level most improves the odds.
action_plan.evidence: Games campaigns asking goal <= $5,000 funded at 55% vs a 40% baseline (lift 1.36, n=9,834). Funded campaigns here had a median goal of $5,000 vs $10,000 for failed.

action_plan.action: Add a number to your title (e.g. an edition or volume number)
action_plan.why: Title framing is a cheap signal the model associates with funded campaigns.
action_plan.evidence: Games campaigns with a number in the title funded at 59% vs a 40% baseline (lift 1.46, n=2,823).

action_plan.action: Launch on Tuesday instead of Thursday
action_plan.why: Launch timing is a near-zero-cost lever — the funded cohort clusters on specific weekdays.
action_plan.evidence: Games campaigns launched on Tuesday funded at 50% vs a 40% baseline (lift 1.24, n=5,071).
